content:
GrainQL runs a [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server. An AI assistant that connects to it can ask questions of your analytics data, the same questions you ask in the dashboard. No custom integration is required. MCP is an open protocol that lets a language model call external tools.

## What an assistant can do

| Task | What the assistant does | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| Explore the schema | Lists every event your site tracks and the dimensions you can filter by. | `mcp:read` |
| Run queries | Breakdowns, time series, counts, and period-over-period comparisons, with the same surprise detection that Neo uses in the dashboard. | `mcp:query` |
| Investigate a drop | Clusters sessions, compares segments, analyzes Tracks (start to goal funnels), and correlates events. | `mcp:investigate` |
| Write a digest | Summarizes what changed in your tenant for a day or a week, ready to paste into Slack or Notion. | `mcp:query` |

Read [Tools](/ai-tools/mcp/tools) for every tool and its inputs.

## Endpoint

## MCP endpoint

`https://www.grainql.com/api/mcp`

This is the only URL you paste into a client. The server speaks MCP over Streamable HTTP. A client discovers the OAuth flow on its first connection.

Include `www`. The `grainql.com` address without `www` redirects, and MCP clients drop the sign-in token on that redirect. The client then connects but shows no tools.

## The OAuth flow

GrainQL is its own OAuth 2.1 authorization server. When an MCP client calls the endpoint without a token, this happens:

1

The client asks GrainQL what it needs

GrainQL responds `401` with a `WWW-Authenticate` header that points at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`.

2

The client registers itself

The client calls `/oauth/register` (RFC 7591 Dynamic Client Registration) and receives a public, PKCE-only `client_id`. There are no shared secrets.

3

You approve in the browser

GrainQL opens a consent screen. You choose **All workspaces in my account**, or **Select workspaces** and tick the ones the assistant will see. You read the scopes that the client asks for. A workspace on the consent screen is a tenant.

4

The client receives a token

After you click **Authorize**, the client receives a short-lived `mcpat_…` access token and an `mcprt_…` refresh token. Both are scoped to the workspaces you chose.

You can revoke any client at [Settings, MCP clients](https://grainql.com/dashboard/settings/mcp). If you do not want to give an assistant access to production data yet, create a test tenant and connect the assistant to that tenant first.

## Scopes

GrainQL has three scopes. A client asks for the scopes it needs at authorize time. The consent screen shows every scope in plain English before you approve.

| Scope | Grants | Example question |
|---|---|---|
| `mcp:read` | Event list, dimension discovery, integration health | ”Is tracking wired up?” |
| `mcp:query` | Query, count, compare, digest | ”Signups by country last week?” |
| `mcp:investigate` | Segment compare, session cluster, track analyze, correlate event | ”Why did checkout drop on Tuesday?” |

Read [Security and scopes](/ai-tools/mcp/security) for what each scope unlocks and how tokens are stored.

## Clients

## Claude

Claude.ai on the web, Claude Desktop, and Claude Code.

## Cursor

The Cursor editor and its agent.

## ChatGPT

Developer Mode on the Pro, Team, Enterprise, and Edu plans.

## Tools

The tool reference for any other MCP client.

## Limits

| Limit | Value | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Backend calls | 16 per MCP request | Every tool call. `grain_query_compare` counts as 2. |
| Tenants per token | 1 | Every `mcpat_…` token. Chosen at consent. |
| Preview window | 7 days | The consent screen. |

If an agent reaches the budget, it receives a structured error. The agent then asks you to narrow the question.

## Safety

- Every token carries exactly one `tenantId`, chosen at consent. An assistant cannot cross tenants in a session.
- Version 1 is read-only. No tool writes, deletes, or changes data. You can grant `mcp:investigate` without a risk that the assistant changes a segment definition.
- GrainQL encrypts upstream tokens with AES-GCM before it writes them to the database. GrainQL stores its own tokens only as SHA-256 hashes.
